How well a varpro fit tested each variable

Source: R/varpro_coverage.R
varpro_coverage.Rd

Reports, for every term varpro could test, how many of the forest's trees hold a usable release rule for it, next to its importance z. Use it to tell a variable that was tested and found unimportant from one that was barely tested at all.

Usage

varpro_coverage(
  object,
  by = c("term", "variable"),
  trim = 0.1,
  max.tree = object$rf$ntree,
  max.rules.tree = object$max.rules.tree,
  noise = NULL,
  kind_values = 5L,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A fitted varpro object.

by

"term" (one row per term in the fit's data, factor levels separately) or "variable" (one-hot levels rolled up to their original variable: tested in a tree when any level is, z the largest level z).

trim

Coverage below which a term counts as untested, and the winsorisation trim used for z. Defaults to 0.1, as in varPro::importance(): the share of trees below which z is 0.

max.tree

Number of trees to score. Defaults to every tree, rather than varPro's sample of 150, so that coverage rests on all the evidence. Coverage and z always come from the same extracted rules.

max.rules.tree

Maximum release rules sampled per tree; defaults to the value stored in object. Sampling only happens in trees with more branches than this.

noise

NULL, or a regular expression matching the names of noise variables (for example "^noise").

kind_values

A numeric variable with at most this many distinct values counts as categorical for the noise comparison.

seed

Seed passed to varPro::varpro.strength(), which samples the release rules; with a seed (or a set.seed() call first) the table is reproducible.

Value

A data frame of class c("varpro_coverage", "data.frame"), one row per term (or variable), most-covered first, with columns term (term rows only), variable, n_terms (variable rows only), eligible (varpro built rules for it; FALSE when the split weights or nvar cut it first), n_trees (trees with a usable rule), coverage (n_trees over trees scored), n_rules (usable rules), z (computed as varPro::importance() computes it, with its default local.std = TRUE, from the same rules; NA when never returned) and tested (coverage >= trim). With noise set it adds noise (logical), kind, noise_cut and selected (a tested real row whose z beats noise_cut). Attributes by, trees, trim and max.rules.tree record the settings.

Why coverage matters

varPro::importance() scores a term by a trimmed (winsorised) mean of its importance in each tree, and a tree without a usable release rule for the term counts as zero. A term tested in fewer than about trim of the trees therefore has every non-zero value trimmed away and comes back with z exactly 0: it is untested, not unimportant. A term varpro does not return at all was never tested, either because it was cut before rule-building (split weights and nvar) or because no rule had cases on both sides of its release. Neither is evidence of no effect.

A rule is usable when its out-of-bag region and its released complement both hold cases. Coverage is the share of scored trees with at least one usable rule for the term.

Noise reference

varpro's default cutoff (z > 0.79) does not carry from one fit to another with the default local.std = TRUE: z is then an unstandardised mean, and it shrinks as more terms share each tree. If the data include permuted copies of real columns (noise by construction), name them with a common prefix and pass a pattern as noise. Each real row is then compared with the largest z among tested noise rows of the same kind (categorical or continuous); an untested noise row has z = 0 by construction and sets no bar. A kind with no tested noise falls back to the largest tested-noise z overall. ggRandomForests does not add the noise columns; do that before fitting.

See also

gg_varpro, varpro_feature_names

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("varPro", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(20261014)
  d <- mtcars
  d$noise_wt <- sample(d$wt)        # permuted copy: noise by construction
  vp <- varPro::varpro(mpg ~ ., data = d, ntree = 50)
  set.seed(20261014)
  varpro_coverage(vp, noise = "^noise")
}
#> Warning: no noise variable was tested (coverage >= trim), so the noise check is empty: noise_cut is 0 and every tested row is selected.
